Office Visit - Follow-up
Patient: Emil Ivanova | DOB: 07/25/1980 | MRN: SYN-3329984
Date of service: 02/01/2025 | Dr. Gwen Northcott, MD

History of present illness:
44-year-old man seen for follow-up of low back pain. He first noticed the pain shooting down his left leg after a weekend of gardening, nearly four months before this visit.

Treatment to date:
Two months of supervised exercise sessions plus over-the-counter anti-inflammatories have not brought lasting relief.

History:
Past medical history: hypothyroidism, gastroesophageal reflux.
Medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; omeprazole 20 mg daily.

Review of systems:
No trouble controlling urine or stool, no numbness in the groin area, no fevers, stable weight, and no prior malignancy.

Physical exam:
Back: tenderness over the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles; straight-leg raise positive on the left at 30 degrees.
He struggles to walk on his heels on the left, ankle jerks are equal, and touch feels dull across the top of the left foot.

Assessment and plan:
Assessment: left L5 lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation; home exercise program; follow up after imaging.
